title: Does a consumer subscription with training disabled satisfy the third-party LLM conditions?

latest.raw:
The guidance asks for provider terms with no training on inputs or outputs, no rights taken in either, and retention limited in time and purpose. The example given is "Anthropic API, Claude Sonnet, commercial terms, no training on customer content".

We used a consumer subscription (Claude Max) with the "Help improve our AI models" setting off, and did not rate any outputs. The no-training condition is met by that setting. We cannot verify the "no rights taken by the provider" clause for consumer terms against the commercial terms in your example.

Does a consumer tier with training disabled satisfy the conditions, or do you require a commercial/API tier specifically? Happy to record whichever answer you give in the methods description.

latest.raw:
Hello,
Thanks for checking. Based on the guidance from our Privacy and Compliance team, Claude Max may be acceptable, but we cannot confirm that simply having "Help improve our AI models" turned off is sufficient.
The requirement is that the service does not train on or otherwise take rights in the inputs/outputs, and that any retention is limited in time and purpose. These requirements apply regardless of whether the service is a consumer subscription or an API/commercial tier.
If the Claude Max terms applicable to your account meet those conditions, then use of Claude Max would be consistent with the guidance. Please document the provider, tier, relevant settings, and applicable data-handling terms in your methods description.
If you are unable to verify those terms for the consumer plan, we would recommend using an API/commercial offering for which the applicable data-handling terms are explicit.
Best,
Gaia
